title: Strict HTTP/1 chunked-frame parser repair
hypothesis: Repairing a realistic parser can require keeping a byte cursor synchronized across valid chunk framing, extensions, trailers, malformed line endings, and a following pipelined message.
why_hard: Rejecting one malformed line is insufficient if valid frames consume too much or too little input. The correct repair must preserve the next message boundary as well as parse the current payload.
next_action: Design a small existing-parser fixture with a complete byte-consumption contract and bounded independent grammar checks; assess whether the repair remains substantive before authoring a trial.

sources.note: Recorded public Go framing incident involving bare LF in chunk-size lines and composition risk. Proposed task is an isolated parser repair with no real service.

notes: An untested design proposal from the initial shortlist. The recorded difficulty and runtime ratings are estimates. Keep it a repair with observable message boundaries; a regex-only exercise would lose the proposed reasoning core.
